workingDefinitionFrozenBeforeReview: Opening setup is the first transfer after an in-bounds pull is caught or picked up, when that transfer hands the disc to the player who starts the offense. It need not move toward the middle. If the pull receiver attacks directly, including when the defense prevents an opening transfer, recorded throw 1 is already attacking. After one confirmed setup transfer, all later passes count as attacking, including handler weaves, resets, and passes to an open handler. For a confirmed brick or sideline restart, or a later possession after a turnover, count the first pass as attacking. Bringing a turnover to the goal line or tapping it in does not create a pull setup. A failed setup attempt remains a turnover in the full-possession record; it can have zero attacking throws. Caught-versus-grounded pull handling may be unclear even when setup is clear. A penalty before the first brick-start pass does not turn that pass into setup. Use an uncertain label when the film does not settle the distinction. Opening setup is a working expectation with explicit exceptions, not a reason to remove every opening pass automatically.
classificationStatus: All twelve human reviews archived; Austin immediate attack confirmed in chat. These are fresh-game definition checks, not league prevalence or an automatic-classifier accuracy estimate. Any definition change based on them makes them development cases for that revised rule.
rules: Preserve all existing reviews. Keep film availability, pass sequence and setup classification separate. Do not infer setup from coordinates.
